title: Henselian reduction preserves and reflects w-strict locality
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. A commutative ring $B$ is w-strictly local [sk-def-pe-wlocal] when the set of closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is closed, every point specializes to exactly one closed point, and every localization $B_{\mathfrak m}$ at a maximal ideal is strictly henselian. Then $A$ is w-strictly local if and only if $A/I$ is w-strictly local.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.13, with the local-ring characterization in Lemma 2.2.9

proof.text: Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $R=A/I$ and $Z=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The henselian factorization criterion gives $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(A)$. Identify $Z$ with $V(I)\subseteq X$: inverse image along $A\to R$ bijects primes of $R$ with primes of $A$ containing $I$, with inverse $\mathfrak p\mapsto\mathfrak p/I$, and takes $D(\bar a)$ to $D(a)\cap V(I)$. These formulas prove the homeomorphism. Maximal ideals correspond because all maximal ideals of $A$ contain $I$ and $R/(\mathfrak m/I)=A/\mathfrak m$. Thus $Z^c=X^c$ as subsets of $X$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.13, closed points and locality along the quotient

proof.text: Assume first that $A$ is w-strictly local. The subset $Z^c=X^c$ is closed in $Z$, because it is closed in $X$. If $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ is a prime of $R$, its inverse image $\mathfrak p$ is contained in exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. Containment is preserved and reflected by the quotient correspondence, so $\bar{\mathfrak p}$ is contained in exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$ of $R$. This proves w-locality of $R$ directly from the definition.

For each maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, the ring $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian. The quotient-localization isomorphism is $R_{\mathfrak m/I}\cong A_{\mathfrak m}/IA_{\mathfrak m}$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, the ideal $IA_{\mathfrak m}$ lies in the maximal ideal, so the strictly henselian quotient lemma applies. All maximal localizations of $R$ are therefore strictly henselian. Together with the preceding step this proves that $R$ is w-strictly local.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.15, local-ring argument for the forward implication of Lemma 2.2.13

proof.text: Now assume $R$ is w-strictly local. Its closed-point subset is closed in $Z$, hence $X^c=Z^c$ is closed in $X$ because $Z=V(I)$ is closed. For any prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$, the henselian connectedness lemma makes $C=V(\mathfrak p+I)$ a nonempty connected subset of $Z$. The component lemma supplies a continuous retraction $r:Z\to Z^c$ onto a profinite space. Its image $r(C)$ is a singleton: otherwise two points are separated by a clopen subset of the profinite space, disconnecting $C$. Every maximal ideal of $A$ containing $\mathfrak p$ belongs to $C$, since it contains $I$, and is fixed by $r$. Moreover, for any $q\in C$, its closed specialization $r(q)$ still contains $\mathfrak p$, so there is such a maximal ideal. Hence there is exactly one. Together with closedness of $X^c$, this proves w-locality of $A$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.13, use of Lemma 2.1.7; its component argument expanded using Stacks Tag 09Y6

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary faithfully flat etale $A$-algebra $B$. Faithful flatness makes $\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ surjective. Apply etale-covering base change to the singleton covering and $Z\to X$: the projection $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}B\to Z$ is etale and surjective. By the affine fibre-product identification this fibre product is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_AB)$ with first projection $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $r\mapsto r\otimes1$; with $\bar B=B/IB=R\otimes_A B$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}\bar B\to Z$ is therefore etale and surjective. The displayed algebra identification follows by sending $\bar a\otimes b$ to $ab$ modulo $IB$, with inverse $b\bmod IB\mapsto 1\otimes b$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.13, base change of the faithfully flat etale algebra

proof.text: For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $R$, base change this etale surjection to $\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak n}$. It remains an etale surjection, so there is a point above its closed point. The ring $R_{\mathfrak n}$ is strictly henselian by the hypothesis on $R$; the strictly henselian etale-neighbourhood section lemma gives a section over $\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak n}$. By the affine spectrum correspondence it gives an $R$-algebra map $\bar B\to R_{\mathfrak n}$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.9, sections over the local rings at closed points

proof.text: The affine etale criterion says that $\bar B$ is finitely presented as an $R$-algebra. Apply the finitely presented localization factorization theorem to $\bar B\to R_{\mathfrak n}$ with multiplicative set $R\setminus\mathfrak n$. It gives $f_{\mathfrak n}\notin\mathfrak n$ and an $R$-algebra map $\bar B\to R_{f_{\mathfrak n}}$. Because this is an $R$-algebra map it is a section on the whole principal open $D(f_{\mathfrak n})$; there is no additional section equation to descend.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.9, spreading out by finite presentation

proof.text: The principal opens just obtained cover $Z^c$. By the component lemma, the space $Z$, w-local in the sense of the w-strict-locality definition, is w-local in the sense used by the w-local partition lemma, and $Z^c$ is profinite. Its profiniteness gives a finite clopen partition subordinate to this cover: choose a clopen neighbourhood inside a covering open at each point, take a finite subcover by compactness, and replace it by successive differences. The w-local partition lemma extends that partition uniquely to a finite clopen partition of $Z$, whose parts lie in the corresponding principal opens, because those opens contain the corresponding components. Restrict the local sections to these parts and glue them. The parts are disjoint, so there are no overlap equations. This is a global section of $\operatorname{Spec}\bar B\to Z$, or equivalently an $R$-algebra map $\rho_0:\bar B\to R$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.9, gluing the sections using w-locality

proof.text: Compose $B\to\bar B$ with $\rho_0$ to obtain an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:B\to A/I$. The affine etale criterion gives finite presentation, $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{B/A}=0$. The zero module is finite projective (a summand of the rank-zero free module), so the definition of a smooth ring map shows that $B$ is smooth over $A$. Apply henselian smooth-algebra lifting with base ring $A$, smooth algebra $B$, target algebra $A$ and the original ideal $I$. It gives an $A$-algebra map $\rho:B\to A$ lifting $\sigma$. Such a map is a retraction of the structural map by its $A$-linearity: $\rho(a\cdot1)=a$.

source.place: Tag 0H74, lemma-lift-smooth-henselian; lifting step of BS Lemma 2.2.13

proof.text: The algebra $B$ in step 5 was arbitrary, so every faithfully flat etale $A$-algebra has an $A$-algebra retraction. The split-etale-cover maximal-local criterion now implies that every maximal localization $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is strictly henselian. Combine this with w-locality proved in step 4 and the definition of w-strict locality. Thus $A$ is w-strictly local whenever $A/I$ is, completing the equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 2.2.13, 2.2.9 and 2.2.15; topology expanded with Stacks 09Y6, lifting via 0H74, and recognition via 097V
